sentences.text: P. V. KUNHIKRISHNAN, J.
The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.113/2011 on the file of the Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, Thalassery.
The above case was charge sheeted against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused married one Roopini on 27.11.2005 and they live together as husband and wife along with their son Gokul in a rented house and during that period,
the accused ill treated Roopini for dowry and demanded her to be a surrogate mother for another.

It is alleged that, on account of the continuous ill treatment, Roopini committed suicide in between 5 a.m and 9.30p.m. on 18.08.2010 after throwing her son in the well situated in the property of one 2024:KER:61142 Raveendran and as a result of the same, she and her son died.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offences.
3. Based on the final report, the trial against the petitioner started.
PWs.1 to 25 were examined on the side of the prosecution.
Exts.P1 to P27, P2(a) were marked on the side of the prosecution.
MO1 to MO6, MO7 series, MO8 and MO9 series were marked as material objects.
After closing the prosecution evidence, the accused was examined under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
Thereafter, the prosecution and accused were heard under Section 232 Cr.P.C.
Since there is no reason for acquitting the accused, the accused was called upon to enter on his defense and adduce evidence.
But the accused has not adduced any evidence.
Thereafter, the case was posted for judgment.

Subsequently, the learned Assistant Sessions Judge passed an order on 07.12.2016 observing that the charge is to be altered by adding the offence punishable under Section 304B IPC and the procedure to be followed under Section 217 Cr.P.C.
Hence the prosecution and the accused were directed to file memo stating the witness to be recalled and examined.
Aggrieved by the order dated 07.12.2016, this Criminal 2024:KER:61142 Miscellaneous Case is filed.

4. Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
5.
The counsel for the petitioner submitted that the impugned order is illegal and unsustainable.
The counsel submitted that, no witness had deposed about any dowry demand in this case.
The counsel submitted that, in such circumstances, the learned Magistrate erred in passing an order to alter the charge by adding the offence under Section 304B IPC.
The counsel submitted that the impugned order is unsustainable.
The Public Prosecutor supported the impugned order.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that, in the facts and circumstances of the case Section 304B IPC is also attracted.
Therefore, learned Additional Assistant Sessions Judge perfectly justified in passing the impugned order.

sentences.text: This Court considered the contention of the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
This Court perused the impugned order also.
The petitioner filed a detailed argument note also.
This Court perused the same also.
It is an admitted fact that the charge was originally framed under Sections 498A and 306 IPC.
The learned Additional Assistant Sessions Judge decided to add Section 304B for the reasons stated in paragraphs 8 and 9 of Annexure-A3.

The same is extracted hereunder:
'8.
It is an admitted fact that the death of Roopini, the deceased wife of the accused was on 18- 08-2010 and the date of their marriage was 27-11- 2005.
It is also proved and admitted that the death was in unnatural circumstances as Roopini committed suicide after killing her son.

So, the unnatural death of Roopini within 7 years of her marriage coupled with the allegation of the prosecution that she was subjected to matrimonial cruelty with the demand for dowry prima facie attracts the offence punishable U/s.304B of IPC.
How far the prosecution will succeed in proving its case for all or any of the offences need not be gone into at this stage.
It is the duty of the court to frame a charge for any other offence/s than the one with which the accused is charged, if such offence is made out prima facie.
9. True that an offence U/S.304B of IPC is punishable with imprisonment for life and the minimum sentence provided for is 7 years.
Likewise, the offences punishable U/s.304B and 498A of IPC are distinct and mutually not inclusive as held in the decision reported in (2008)3 SCC (Cri.)915(supra).
In 2024:KER:61142 fact, the same necessitates the framing of a separate charge for the offence punishable U/s.304B of IPC as well.
Otherwise, there will be miscarriage of justice.

The failure on the part of the Investigating Officer and the omission on the part of the court in framing the charge for the above offence earlier also will not stand in the way of the court in exercising the power conferred by S.216 of Cr.P.C.

So, the court is of the considered view that the charge is to be altered by adding the offence punishable U/s.304B of IPC as well and the procedure to be followed as provided in S.217 Cr.P.C will be adhered to.

The prosecution and the accused shall file memo stating the witnesses to be recalled and examined, if any, on their sides, after reading over the altered charge.'
8.
The learned Sessions Judge observed that since the unnatural death of Roopini happened within 7 years of her marriage with the petitioner, Section 304B IPC is attracted.
I think there cannot be any presumption like that.

Of course as per Section 113A of the Indian Evidence Act, there is a presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married women, in which, it is stated that when the question is whether the commission of suicide by a woman had been abetted by her husband or any relative of her husband and it is shown that she had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her 2024:KER:61142 marriage and that her husband or such relative of her husband had subjected her to cruelty, the court may presume, having regard to all the other Panniyodan Keloth Gijith vs State Of Kerala on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187748405/
3 circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband.

sentences.text: The presumption as to dowry death is dealt in Section 113B of the Evidence Act which is extracted hereunder:

'Presumption as to dowry death:
When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry,
the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.'

9. If a person has committed a dowry death of a women and it is shown that soon before her death,
such women had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with,
any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.

The explanation to Section 113B of the Evidence Act says that for the purpose of this Section 'dowry death' shall have the same meaning as in Section 304B IPC.
2024:KER:61142 10.

Therefore, to presume dowry death, it should be shown that, soon before the death, such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
Therefore, cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with any demand for dowry is necessary to presume dowry death as per Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act.
The learned Additional Assistant Sessions Judge has not considered these aspects while deciding the matter.
11. The learned Public Prosecutor made available the Case Diary in this case and also the suicide note of the deceased.
This Court perused the suicide note also.
There is nothing in the suicide note also to show that there was any demand for dowry.
I don't want to make any further opinion about the same because there are other averments in the suicide note which is to be decided in the main case.

Unless there is evidence adduced by the prosecution about the demand for dowry, there cannot be any presumption that the accused committed the offence under Section 304B IPC.
2024:KER:61142 12.

According to the petitioner, even the entire evidence adduced by the prosecution would not show that there is any demand for dowry, I think this aspect has to be reconsidered by the learned Additional Assistant Sessions Judge.

To facilitate the learned Additional Assistant Sessions Judge to reconsider the matter, I am of the considered opinion that the order dated 07.12.2016 in S.C.
No.113/2011 is to be set aside.

Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is allowed in the following manner:
a) The order dated 07.12.2016 in S.C. No.113/2011 on the file of the Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, Thalassery is set aside.
